portrayal: The necessity for fiction was probably born of the problem of taboo on certain revelations. It was not only a need of the imagination but an answer to the limitations placed on portrayal of others.
portents:
A woman who writes feels too much,
those trances and portents!
As if cycles and children and islands
weren't enough; as if mourners and gossips
and vegetables were never enough.
She thinks she can warm the stars.
A writer is essentially a spy.
Dear love, I am that girl.
pornography: Pornography is a direct denial of the power of the erotic, for it represents the suppression of true feeling. Pornography emphasizes sensation without feeling.
portrait: I had no portrait, now, but am small, like the Wren, and my Hair is bold, like the Chestnut Bur — and my eyes, like the Sherry in the Glass, that the Guest leaves — Would this do just as well?
Letter to T. W. Higginson (July 1862); Letters (1958) p. 411, no. 268
port:
Wild nights - Wild nights!
Were I with thee
Wild nights should be
Our luxury!
Futile - the winds -
To a Heart in port -
Done with the Compass -
Done with the Chart!
Rowing in Eden -
Ah - the Sea!
Might I but moor - tonight -
In thee!
portugal:
Oh salty sea, how much of your salt
are tears of Portugal!

Oh Portugal, today you are fog...
The Hour has come!

The sea is fulfilled, and the Empire fell apart.
Lord, Portugal must yet fulfill itself!
portuguese:
The sea with an end can be Greek or Roman:
the endless sea is Portuguese.
I don't write in Portuguese. I write myself.
My homeland is the Portuguese language.

porous: Make your ego porous. Will is of little importance, complaining is nothing, fame is nothing. Openness, patience, receptivity, solitude is everything.
